test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Jawaharlal Nehru classified which of the following Acts as ‘a new charter of slavery’?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Government of India Act, 1935.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Act introduced **provincial autonomy,** granting limited self-governance to provinces while maintaining British control over critical matters.
 
• It established a **bicameral legislature** at the center with the Federal Assembly and the Council of States, marking a significant shift in governance.
 
• The Act proposed a **federal structure with provinces**, princely states, and British India, though the federation** never **fully came into effect.
 
• It introduced **dyarchy** at the central level, dividing subjects into "Federal" and "Provincial" categories, but retaining key powers with the British.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Charter Act, 1853:**

 
 
• This Act separated the **legislative and executive** functions of the Governor-General's Council.
 
• It introduced an open competition for the recruitment of **civil servants.**
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act (1919):**
 
 
• It is also known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act.
 
• it allowed the British government to imprison individuals suspected of sedition without trial for up to two years.
 
• The Act led to widespread protests across India, including the infamous **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** in 1919.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms):**
 
 
• This Act introduced **dyarchy** at the provincial level, dividing subjects into "Transferred" and "Reserved" categories, with Indian ministers responsible for the former.
 
• It expanded the legislative councils at both the central and provincial levels, but the franchise remained limited to a small, **privileged section** of the population.
